approachQuestion.prompt:
Shared floor coverage

Two axis-aligned closed rectangles are given as (left,bottom,right,top), with left<=right and bottom<=top. Return the area they cover in common. A degenerate rectangle, edge contact or point contact has area zero.

Example 1: A=(0,0,4,3),B=(2,1,6,5) -> 4.
Example 2: A=(0,0,1,1),B=(1,0,2,1) -> 0.
Example 3: A=(0,0,1,1),B=(2,2,3,3) -> 0.

Constraints and assumptions: Coordinates are integers in [-10^9,10^9]. Return exact integer area in signed 64-bit; include edge and point contacts as zero area. Choose the best time bound among the offered correct methods, then the least auxiliary storage when time ties.

options.text: Intersect horizontal and vertical coordinate intervals independently, clamp each overlap length to zero, and multiply the lengths.
options.feedback: A point belongs to both rectangles exactly when both coordinate memberships hold. Clamping prevents disjoint projections from creating a false positive area.

options.text: Multiply min(rights)-max(lefts) by min(tops)-max(bottoms) without clamping.
options.feedback: For A=(0,0,1,1),B=(2,2,3,3) both spans are -1, so it returns 1 although the rectangles are disjoint.

options.text: Return the area of the smallest rectangle containing both inputs.
options.feedback: For A=B=(0,0,1,1) this happens to work, but A=(0,0,1,1),B=(2,0,3,1) gives 3 rather than 0.

options.text: Return the area of B if B's lower-left corner is in A, and return zero otherwise.
options.feedback: For A=(0,0,4,3),B=(2,1,6,5), the corner is inside but only area 4 overlaps, not all 16 of B.

feedback.reason: Intersect coordinate projections and clamp disjoint spans before taking an area.
details: The overlap width and height are independent one-dimensional intersections. Clamp each to zero before multiplication so separated rectangles cannot produce a positive area from two negative gaps. Touching edges have zero area.

“Intersect horizontal and vertical coordinate intervals independently, clamp each overlap length to zero, and multiply the lengths.”: A point belongs to both rectangles exactly when both coordinate memberships hold. Clamping prevents disjoint projections from creating a false positive area.
“Multiply min(rights)-max(lefts) by min(tops)-max(bottoms) without clamping.”: For A=(0,0,1,1),B=(2,2,3,3) both spans are -1, so it returns 1 although the rectangles are disjoint.
“Return the area of the smallest rectangle containing both inputs.”: For A=B=(0,0,1,1) this happens to work, but A=(0,0,1,1),B=(2,0,3,1) gives 3 rather than 0.
“Return the area of B if B's lower-left corner is in A, and return zero otherwise.”: For A=(0,0,4,3),B=(2,1,6,5), the corner is inside but only area 4 overlaps, not all 16 of B.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (clamped-span-product). Let C be the coordinate magnitude bound. Choose its tightest standard worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
Include initialization and any copying; no hidden preprocessing or cache.

feedback.reason: A fixed number of endpoint extrema and one product gives overlap area.
details: Only a fixed number of minima, maxima, differences and one multiplication are needed. Width and height are at most 2*10^9, so their product is at most 4*10^18 and fits signed 64-bit. No coordinate enumeration or allocation occurs.
Exact signed 64-bit integer arithmetic, casting before calculations; arithmetic and comparisons cost one unit. No arbitrary-precision operations.
Iterative method, no recursion or hashing, no input copies. Auxiliary space includes all temporary state and buffers, excluding supplied input and returned output.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Correct: two interval intersections and a product.
“O(C + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This would scan coordinates; the method uses arithmetic endpoints.
“O((C + 1)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: No unit cells are enumerated.
“O(1) time, O(C + 1) auxiliary space”: No span or cell table is allocated.
